channel.description: Recent content in Home on Future Feedstocks for Functional Materials

item.title: Innovative valorisation of aquatic plants from the Danube region in a decentralised biorefinery
item.description: Aquatic plants from the Alte and Neue Donau in Vienna and reed from Lake Neusiedl are turned into specialty papers, textile fibres, food trays and packaging – processed close to where they are harvested.

item.title: Marco Beaumont
item.description: Marco Beaumont is a chemist at the Institute of Chemistry of Renewable Resources and leads the F4M group. His work focuses on sustainable chemical routes to cellulose and chitin nanomaterials and on turning underused biomass into functional materials.

item.title: Underused biomass and decentralised biorefineries
item.description: Aquatic plants, reed, straw, bagasse and other residues as starting points for materials – processed close to where they arise.

item.title: Green modification of cellulose, chitin and lignin
item.description: Selective chemistry in water or without solvents that changes just enough of a biopolymer to unlock a new function.

item.title: Sustainable transformation of food loss into processable materials
item.description: Agricultural residues such as maize straw and sugarcane bagasse are selectively esterified into mouldable, nanofibre-reinforced bioplastics – keeping the cellulose nanofibres intact.

item.title: Enzymatically recyclable, sustainable 3D-printable composites for the circular economy
item.description: Bio-based composites for high-resolution stereolithography 3D printing that can be broken down chemically or enzymatically after use – “degradation on demand”.

item.title: Nanocellulose and nanochitin materials
item.description: Nanofibrils, soft nanoparticles, hydrogels, aerogels, films and nanopapers assembled from bio-based building blocks.

item.title: Chitin–protein composites from insects
item.description: Insect farming produces chitin and protein side streams – we tune their ratio to tailor the material properties.

item.title: Nanocellulose from Brazilian biodiversity as biomedical scaffolds for 3D cell culture
item.description: Nanocellulose aerogels from the native Brazilian fibres curauá and piaçaba as scaffolds for neural cell culture – an Austrian–Brazilian cooperation.

item.title: Bioplastics, 3D printing and biomedical materials
item.description: From nanofibre-reinforced thermoplastics and recyclable 3D-printing resins to packaging, food trays and scaffolds for cell culture.
